To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the collective behavior of a large population of neurons with long membrane time constants and balanced synaptic activations can be strongly influenced by the synchronous discharge of a fraction of the neurons in the population.

the thalamocorectal system can be simulated by a model based on realistic connectivity and physiology; the model can reproduce the fast synchronous activity observed in the thalamocortex; and the synchrony of firing within thalamocortex and corticocortex plays a causal role at the system level.

1) thalamocortico-thalamo-cortical loops can produce episodes of synchronous firing in the absence of external stimuli; 2) the firing rate and selectivity of cortical neurons are affected by the synchrony of firing in these loops; and 3) these effects are due to the cooperative and competitive interactions among neurons in these loops.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of firing synchrony in the thalamocorticocortical network of the cat visual system.
the dynamic consequences of synchrony of firing within the thalamocorecortical system.
the role of neural dynamics in the generation of cortical activity patterns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural dynamics in the model are strongly influenced by the firing synchrony of the neurons.
synchrony per se has a causal role in thalamocortically based pattern recognition.

firing synchrony is a significant determinant of the dynamic properties of the thalamo-cortical system, and that the effects of synchronizing the firing of neurons can be understood in terms of the anatomy and physiology of thalamocortically linked neural circuits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
synchrony per se has an important effect on the operation of the system.
the thalamus and the cortex are functionally coupled by synchronous activity.
the neural dynamics in a model for the thalamocorticocortical system are strongly influenced by firing synchrony within the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to the traditional view of neuronal synchrony as a correlate of function, it may be viewed as a fundamental mechanism for the generation of cortical responses.
, at the system level, the effects of synchronizing action potentials in a population of neurons depend on the specific network architecture and on the dynamics of the network.
, in the thalamocoptical system, firing synchrony is a causal factor in shaping the responses of the neurons to visual stimuli, and is not merely an epiphenomenon.
